steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F ( 200 degrees C ). Coat a 15x10x1-inch jelly roll pan with nonstick spray.

Combine brown sugar and eggs in a heavy saucepan; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until sugar is dissolved. Remove from heat. Stir in flour, pecans, vanilla, and salt until well combined; transfer mixture to the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Cool completely on a wire rack, then cut into 36 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandma’s Chew Bread
raw_recipe.description: Grandma’s chew bread recipe is a 6-ingredient Southern-style bar cookie made with brown sugar and crunchy pecans and easy enough for a beginner baker.
raw_recipe.name: Grandma’s Chew Bread

review.reviewBody: I needed a quick recipe and pulled this one up from my recipe files. To my surprise, it was fantastic. I urge everyone to try it.

The problem with this recipe is that the original old fashioned recipe that I remember is called Forty-Niners and it's not 2 cups of flour - its 2 cups of biscuit baking mix. That's where your fat comes from and I never heat the eggs and sugar. I just mix everything together and bake at 325 for 30 - 35 minutes. Don't overbake because you want them chewy! So good!!

I was a bit nervous about how the results would be given the mixed reviews, but these turned out delicious! I made the recipe exactly as written, but made sure to spoon and level the flour (rather than scoop) to avoid them becoming too dense. I also lined the pan with parchment paper (sprayed with nonstick spray) for easy removal and slicing. I will definitely make this one again.
This recipe is missing some sort of fat (sugar isnt fat) like butter or vegetable oil. Add a cup of oil (or equivalent butter). It may be better.

Bread is definitely chewy. I goofed when measuring brown sugar, which comes in a 2 lb bag. Instead of using 1 pound (2 cups), I used 1 cup - really made a difference. Next time I'll use 2 cups from the 2 lb bag. NOTE: rather than cook sugar and eggs in heavy saucepan, I used double boiler - no chance of burning mix if you don't stir all the time. P.S. bread is filling.

Love this recipe, I remember going to my mama(grandmother who raised and adopted me) asking about her recipe told her I had looked all on-line but there wasn't a recipe for "shoe" bread, Mama laughed at me till she had tears in her eyes..miss that woman so bad..she also would make it with crushed walnuts too, and I've used butterscotch pieces instead of chocolate, which was also good

Very delicious ...we added vanilla, chocolate chips ( 1/2 cup sprinkled on top of half of the batter) and extra nuts (1/2 cup extra added to batter ). This is truly a simple but delicious recipe. Thank you for submitting this recipe.

mine did not look like the photo. rather, it looked and tasted more like Blondies. however, I loved it. I made it again using dark brown sugar infused with molasses, and that gave it an extra kick. Great recipe!
Really tasty. Never had anything quite like it. I preferred it cold.. it seemed chewier. Next time I think I'd add more nuts
A pound of sugar is way too much for my taste!
This did not impress me. For one thing don't spray with pam. Butter the pan otherwise it taste greasy to me. Also the pan they recommended was to big. Spread to much, very thin but definitely chewy,
Not the chewbread my family makes. More like a scone or dense muffin you'd hit someone in the head with and knock em out with:/ Taste was there but the consistency is waaaay off!
I did use this recipe and followed all steps and even added an extra step which was I added butter. This recipe is a 10/10 for me.
No changes were made this recipe was not switched we used recipe and it turned out great
This was bland and a weird texture. I thought it would be similar to blondies but they aren't. I thought there would be some flavor with a pound of brown sugar.
Just as made, this recipe is wonderful!! I’ve taken these for years to church dinners, parties, and just family get togethers-and they always get rave reviews! Love them!
Way too much sugar!

I used all purpose flour and did the recipe all to spec except I used a brownie pan. The blondies indeed came out as a bread. These went into the trash. I am toying with recipes and 4 large eggs seemed like a lot and this was proof that indeed, it is. The moisture in the eggs combined with the high temp made for a bad recipe. (Note that I used a non-regulation pan).
There is something missing! It taste horrible. Nothing like the chew bread I know and love. This turned out like a dry and dense bread. No crackle on the top. Can’t serve this at all

I was looking for my old recipe from 30 years ago. The ingredients sounded about the same. I was shocked at 15 min cooking time. 

What I made was not like my old recipe. Wasn’t sweet enough, tasted flour. Not very good. 

My old recipe I remember no cooking sugar, and adding eggs 1 at the time. So for me this was a fail.
